title: Rover Ridge
summary: Slide an ore ruler across a fenced plateau and park it where it just touches: the corner-point method for linear programming.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 12.2, Linear programming problem and its mathematical formulation
concepts: Feasible region and its corner points
Corner point method: the best Z is at a corner
Maximum and minimum with mixed signs
Ties: the best Z along a whole edge
learningOutcome: The student can find the best Z at the corners of a feasible region, spot when there is no maximum or no feasible region, and see when a whole edge is optimal.

levels.title: The richest corner
levels.adds: Baseline: for a bounded region the maximum of Z = ax + by is at a corner point; evaluate Z at each and take the largest (Ex 12.1 Q1, Q2, Q5; Example 1).
hints: List the corner points of the plateau.
Work out Z = ax + by at each corner.
The largest value is the best Z.

levels.title: Mixed signs
levels.adds: New: a minus sign in Z, and a minimum is asked for; the optimum is still at a corner (Ex 12.1 Q2, Q9; Example 4).
hints: Evaluate Z at every corner, carefully with the signs.
The question tells you whether to take the largest or the smallest.
The extreme may not be at the corner that looks best.

levels.title: A bigger plateau
levels.adds: New: five or six corners found by solving pairs of boundary lines from the inequalities alone (Ex 12.1 Q3, Q5, Q8; Examples 2, 3).
hints: Each corner is where two neighbouring boundary lines meet.
Solve each pair of equations to get the corner.
Compare Z at all the corners, not only the first few.

levels.title: Open plains
levels.adds: New: the plateau runs off the map. A minimum can still exist; a maximum may not, and some constraints have no common ground at all (Ex 12.1 Q4, Q9, Q10).
hints: Find the corners, then ask whether the region is closed or runs on forever.
For a maximum on an open region with a, b positive, Z can grow without end.
If two constraints cannot both hold, there is no feasible region.

levels.title: Level ridge
levels.adds: New: when the ruler lies along an edge, every point of that edge is best; say so as well as the value (Ex 12.1 Q6 to Q8).
hints: Work out Z at every corner.
If two neighbouring corners tie for the best, the whole edge between them is best.
The edge is parallel to the ruler: their slopes match.

misconceptions: The best Z is where the biggest x and y are
The best Z can be in the middle of the region
A minimum is always at the origin
